assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin biology, receptor action, proglucagon processing) led to therapies that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with large cardiovascular and metabolic outcome benefits. It is a rare chain from basic physiology to broad clinical impact, with clear originality and lasting significance.
assessment.attribution: Holst established the physiology of the active GLP-1 forms and their secretion; Drucker defined actions and receptor biology of GLP-1 and related peptides; Mojsov contributed to identifying the bioactive peptide, though her credit relative to others is debated. Knudsen's role is chiefly pharmaceutical development and fits a prize only if translation is rewarded; the three-person limit forces a choice.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of mechanistic work, several independent drug classes and large randomized outcome trials. Timing is strongly favorable given the global clinical effect.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Drucker, Holst, Mojsov and Knudsen, and with scientists outside the supplied names, is unresolved.
Whether the committee prefers the physiology or the drug-development contribution is uncertain.
My recollection of the detailed priority history is from memory and not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered CAR-T cells created a new class of living drugs, producing durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukemias and lymphomas and extending to myeloma and other settings. The concept of T cells redirected with synthetic receptors is original and clinically transformative.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain's group developed key CAR design principles including costimulation; June's group led clinical translation with CD19 CAR-T cells. Rosenberg contributed adoptive cell therapy and early CAR work, a plausible competing claim, so choosing two of three is not fully settled. Earlier chimeric-receptor work by others is outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Approved products for several years with consistent independent clinical confirmation. Limits in solid tumors and toxicity do not undermine the core achievement.
uncertainties: Foundational priority of earlier chimeric receptor work outside the credited names.
Rosenberg versus June or Sadelain for the third slot.
Long-term safety, including secondary malignancy signals, is still being evaluated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gives millisecond-scale, cell-type-specific control of neural activity and has become a core method across neuroscience, from circuit mapping to behavior. I weigh it against the whole list on its discovery impact, which is original, widely used and lasting, rather than on field familiarity.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann identified and characterized channelrhodopsins as light-gated channels; Deisseroth led the demonstration and extension of their use in neurons and in vivo. Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenbock also have strong claims, so any three-person prize leaves significant contributors out.
assessment.maturity: Mature: over fifteen years of independent adoption and thousands of confirming studies. Therapeutic applications such as retinal optogenetics are only emerging, but recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Six credited names cannot fit within three laureates; allocation is contentious.
The prize favors discoveries in physiology or medicine, and a research tool may be viewed as less aligned.
Priority disputes over the first neuronal demonstrations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR was discovered as the target of rapamycin and defined a central pathway coordinating cell growth with nutrient and growth-factor signals, with implications for cancer, metabolism, aging and immunosuppression. The discovery is fundamental with strong lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified the TOR genes and established TOR as a conserved growth regulator; Schreiber's work on FKBP12-rapamycin contributed materially to the target's identification. Sabatini's contributions to mTORC1 nutrient sensing are significant, but his credit is complicated by unrelated conduct matters, so I would not include him.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with extensive independent confirmation across species and clinical use of rapalogs, though the clinical benefit of mTOR inhibition is narrower than the basic impact.
uncertainties: Credit split among Hall, Schreiber, Sabatini and other mammalian-TOR discoverers not on the list.
Clinical translation is narrower than the basic science importance.
Details of the priority history are from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing TNF to be a therapeutic target in rheumatoid arthritis, first through mechanistic work on cytokine regulation and then clinical trials of anti-TNF antibody, established biologic therapy for chronic inflammatory disease and has benefited millions of patients across several indications.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini form a coherent pair with a clear joint bench-to-bedside narrative. The identification of TNF and the generation of antibodies by other scientists could be raised, but the supplied credit supports a clean two-person prize.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with decades of clinical use, biosimilars and extensive independent confirmation. Recognition is arguably overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees antibody engineering or TNF discovery by others as needing recognition.
Overlap with related cytokine-targeting work such as IL-6 blockade in the same cycle.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable one and proved the principle of molecularly targeted cancer therapy. Work on resistance and second-generation inhibitors extended the impact.
assessment.attribution: Lydon led the kinase inhibitor chemistry program, Druker championed and conducted clinical development, and Sawyers elucidated resistance mechanisms and extended the approach. Credit is relatively clear, though the discoverers of BCR-ABL itself are outside the credited set.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with long-term survival data and independent confirmation across a class of kinase inhibitors.
uncertainties: Whether a translational drug-development prize fits the committee's emphasis.
Role of the industry chemistry team beyond the named scientists.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent infection and demonstrably reduce cervical precancer and cancer; real-world population data show large declines in disease. This is an important preventive medicine achievement built on a clear original discovery of self-assembling L1 particles.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed the L1 VLP approach; Frazer's group contributed parallel VLP work and early vaccine development. Other contributors outside the supplied names, and priority among groups, are possible sources of dispute.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple licensed vaccines and strong population-level effectiveness data confirmed independently; cancer reduction evidence is accumulating, supporting recognition.
uncertainties: Priority among parallel VLP groups and contributors not on the list.
Longer follow-up for invasive cancer endpoints is still accruing.
Prior recognition of the HPV-cancer link may affect framing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-term potentiation is the best-established cellular model of activity-dependent synaptic plasticity and underpins learning and memory research. The original 1973 observation was original and the NMDA receptor mechanisms added mechanistic depth.
assessment.attribution: Bliss and Lømo made the foundational discovery; Collingridge defined the NMDA receptor dependence of LTP; Morris provided the behavioral link. A fair three-person set is possible, but Morris's claim competes for the third slot.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely confirmed, though whether LTP is the mechanism of memory storage remains debated and the discovery is decades old, which complicates timeliness.
uncertainties: Causal relation between LTP and memory is not fully settled.
Choice between Collingridge and Morris for the third slot.
Age and availability of the original discoverers.
